d: You can see the women stretching out of the loggia and descending down the stairs, curiously hinting towards the Giullare who hangs on his side his purple and in his hand an old skirt.
Ostasio da Polenta enters, through the large courtyard door, in the company of Ser Toldo Berardengo.
Irosus and suspicious Guido's son draws the Notaro towards the ark.
It is heard from the high rooms the song of the women.

You can see the Torrigiano in the gorge, occupied to poke the wood under a steaming boiler. He ordered against the wall the cerbottans, the syphons, the rods of the fortresses and the phalanxes and accumulated around all sorts of worked fires. On the tower, near the mangano, a young Balestrier stands at the lookouts.
Francesca enters the right door and moves along the wall to the pillar that holds the arch.
Paul climbs the steps quickly and turns to the Sister-in-law who has retracted to the wall. The Balestriere returns to the lookout.

The Scianchato appeared by the trapdoor, on the stairs of the tower, all in arms, with a Sardinian rod in his hand. He climbs the steps limping and, as he is on the top, raises up his terrible spit, while the harsh voice slits the clamor.

Francesca runs towards the company that descends along one of the side stairs passing through the crossbows, who leave the work and make silent wings. Gianciotto and Paolo run. Two archers carry the bloody young man with weight. Four archers with long Turquoise accompany him with torches.

You see Francesca in front of the book, in the act of reading. The women sitting on the predelle at the bottom piercing the edges of an overlook, listening to the history; and each door hanging on the belt a little glass full of small pearls and gold strips. The sun of the rising March beats on the zendado chermisino and draws a diffuse glow that lights the faces bowed to the top of the needle. The Schiava is near the windowsill and carefully explores the sky.
Francesca turns to the slave who still spies the sky through the window.
The women break into the room, followed by the musicians. Donella carries four garlandettes of white daffodils, suspended to a golden thread that binds them together.

The two Cognati look, in the first moment, without finding a word, both discoloring. Still they hear the sounds far away for the palagio. From the window the room is inaudible of the day that declines.
You see Francesca sitting in the window compartment, and Malatestino standing in front of you.
The lazy guy gets all in arms... discovers his woman, and goes to her.
Gianciotto opens; and appears on the narrow threshold Malatestino holding in the left hand the torch on and holding, by the loop of a rope ligature, the head of Mountain wrapped in a drape.

You can see Francesca, by means of the disjoining curtains, supine on the bed where she stretched out without undressing. The women, dressed in white, wrapped her face to read white bandages, are seated on the low predelle; and speak softly so as not to arouse the lady. At them, on a scan, are laid four lamps of silver turned off.
Francesca throws a scary cry, jumps out of bed and makes an act of fleeing as chased wildly, shaking her hands on her hips as if to free herself from the grip.
The sound of the closing door is heard. Francesca, alone, moves a few steps towards the door: she stops listening
With the thirst of thirst she throws herself into the lover's arms.

Opened the door, Gianciotto, all in arms and covered with dust, rushes into the furious room, looking with his eyes for his brother. Immediately he realizes that Paul, standing outside the floor with his head and shoulders, divines considered for the layer of the overcoat to an iron of the cataract. Francesca, at that unexpected view, throws a very sharp cry, while the Scianchato makes himself over the adulterous and grabs him by the hair forcing him to go up. The Woman gets to his threatening face.
